title: Virtual Head Attention: Shattering the KV Cache Memory Wall

beats.text: Before you train your next model, see how Virtual Head Attention cuts 84.4% of memory overhead.
beats.visual_focus: A glowing neural network node flickering and dimming as a memory bar fills to red.

beats.text: We are trapped: shrink the cache and intelligence dies; boost quality and compute costs explode into oblivion.
beats.visual_focus: A geometric triangle with labels 'Cache Size', 'Compute FLOPs', and 'Model Quality' collapsing inward.

beats.text: Virtual Head Attention shatters this cycle using two lightweight linear operations to recover head diversity without the bloat.
beats.visual_focus: A complex attention matrix simplifying into two clean, parallel linear transformation lines.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—'starving' and 'choking' actually describe the memory bottleneck well without sounding like a corporate brochure. I didn't swipe because you got straight to the point. However, in Beat 4, you mentioned 'Q Premix and Postmix' like I should already know what those are. I get that they're linear, but how are they actually manipulating the attention heads? It feels like a bit of a black box there.

thriller_metadata.villain_entity: The Impossible Triangle of KV cache bloat
thriller_metadata.physical_analogy: A traffic bottleneck where every car needs its own lane, forcing massive, expensive highway expansions that never actually solve the congestion.
thriller_metadata.paradigm_shift: Linear folding of complex attention logic into standard GQA inference kernels
